data.source_title: Reducing Emergency Department (ED) Boarding Time Through Lean Redesign of the ED-to-Inpatient Admission Pathway: A Single-Center Quality-Improvement Study
data.locator: Methods (study period and cohort flow); Results, Cohort flow and admission cycle time; Table 2 and Table 3. Endpoint: admission order to arrival in inpatient bed.
data.source_setting: Adult ED-to-inpatient admissions at King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Centre, a tertiary hospital; single-center pre/post quality-improvement project.
data.source_n: 435 analyzed encounters (217 baseline, 218 post-intervention) from 500 identified; 65 excluded.
data.quantity: Median admission-order-to-inpatient-bed-arrival cycle time, baseline vs post-intervention
data.source_evidence_basis: EHR-derived patient-level admission cycle time fell from 390 to 175 minutes after a bundled redesign; the paper reports this as a 215-minute (55.1%) decrease. The reported intervention included earlier bed coordination, streamlined testing, and transfer checklist changes.
data.limitations: Single-center pre/post QI association; no causal inference, and the bundled intervention prevents component attribution. COVID testing gate was specific to the study context. These observed medians are not a probability distribution and are not RWJ data.
data.inferred_scenario_use: External reference for admission-to-bed cycle-time scenarios; retain baseline/post as separate contextual benchmarks, and decompose locally into bed request, assignment, EVS, ready signal, handoff, and transport only when local timestamps exist.

data.source_title: Reducing Emergency Department (ED) Boarding Time Through Lean Redesign of the ED-to-Inpatient Admission Pathway: A Single-Center Quality-Improvement Study
data.locator: Results, Monthly Pareto charts; Figures 3A-3C (January-March 2023 delay events).
data.source_setting: Same single-center adult ED admission pathway; monthly operational delay-event tallies.
data.source_n: 86 categorized inefficiency events: January 31, February 31, March 24; event counts, not patient-level cohort denominators.
data.quantity: Share of monthly delay events attributed to bed/receiving-unit readiness categories
data.unit: percent of categorized monthly delay events
data.source_evidence_basis: The paper's operational Pareto tallies identify receiving-unit delay, bed not ready, and last-minute orders as the leading recorded categories in the baseline months.
data.limitations: These are categorized delay events, not unique patients or duration shares; local coding definitions and this hospital's workflows may differ. Monthly denominator is small. Not an RWJ observation.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent admission delays as competing transition blockers (receiving-unit acceptance, bed readiness, late orders); use the reported proportions only as qualitative external prioritization, not local probabilities or time distributions.
